monstera.name: Monstera deliciosa
monstera.shortDescription: Iconic split tropical foliage — a living room focal point.
monstera.description:
Monstera deliciosa is one of the most popular houseplants for city apartments. Large perforated leaves bring a jungle feel without fussy care.

It adapts well to bright indirect light and moderate humidity. With age it forms a sturdy stem you can stake.

Root & Leaf ships it in a ceramic pot with drainage and a short repotting guide.
monstera.watering: Every 7–10 days when the top soil is dry

pothos.name: Golden pothos
pothos.shortDescription: Forgiving trailer — survives corners with no direct sun.
pothos.description:
Golden pothos is a classic for beginners. Tolerates irregular watering and low light.

Grow in a hanging planter or on a shelf — stems trail beautifully. Variegated leaves brighten the room.

Great for studios, bedrooms, or north-facing offices.

sansevieria.name: Snake plant 'Laurentii'
sansevieria.shortDescription: Striped upright leaves — minimal water, maximum style.
sansevieria.description:
Snake plant is the champion of resilience. Handles rare watering, dry air, and low light.

Vertical leaves save space — perfect by the bed or in a narrow hall. Releases oxygen at night.

Ideal for busy city dwellers who travel often.

ficus-lyrata.name: Fiddle-leaf fig
ficus-lyrata.shortDescription: Violin-shaped glossy leaves — a status plant for bright rooms.
ficus-lyrata.description:
Fiddle-leaf fig is an interior designer favorite. Large glossy leaves create drama in a window corner.

Needs stable bright indirect light and careful watering. Dislikes being moved — pick a spot once.

Includes a guide to prevent lower leaf drop.
ficus-lyrata.watering: Weekly when soil is half dry

zz-plant.name: ZZ plant
zz-plant.shortDescription: Glossy dark green leaves — nearly indestructible for offices.
zz-plant.description:
ZZ plant stores water in rhizomes, so forgotten watering is fine. Looks expensive year-round.

Grows under fluorescent light and in room corners. Slow but steady growth.

Recommended for open offices and home desks without south windows.

peace-lily.name: Peace lily
peace-lily.shortDescription: White spathes and glossy leaves — wilts when thirsty.
peace-lily.description:
Peace lily is one of few bloomers for partial shade. White spathes appear several times a year.

Great at removing formaldehyde. If you forget to water, leaves droop but revive within an hour.

Perfect for a humid bathroom.

rubber-plant.name: Rubber plant
rubber-plant.shortDescription: Deep burgundy or green gloss — a vertical room accent.
rubber-plant.description:
Rubber tree forms a strong trunk and wide crown. Varieties like Abidjan and Tineke offer different leaf tones.

Needs a bright spot without harsh midday sun. Wipe leaves monthly with a damp cloth.

Best for rooms with ceilings from 2.5 m.

aloe-vera.name: Aloe vera
aloe-vera.shortDescription: Windowsill succulent — rare water, gel inside leaves.
aloe-vera.description:
Aloe loves a sunny windowsill. Stores water in fleshy leaves — overwatering hurts more than neglect.

Compact for a dresser, kitchen shelf, or home remedy corner.

Shipped in a drainage pot with sandy succulent mix.

spider-plant.name: Spider plant
spider-plant.shortDescription: Striped leaves and “spiderettes” — safe for families with kids.
spider-plant.description:
Spider plant quickly produces baby rosettes on long stolons — easy to propagate.

One of the best natural air filters at home. Non-toxic for cats and dogs.

Looks great in a hanging planter above a desk.

philodendron.name: Heartleaf philodendron
philodendron.shortDescription: Heart-shaped leaves — fast growth and soft tropical vibe.
philodendron.description:
Heartleaf philodendron is a monstera cousin but more compact. Heart leaves on long stems.

Tolerates indirect light and moderate humidity. Train on a rope or shelf.

A boho shelf essential from Brazil.

calathea.name: Calathea orbifolia
calathea.shortDescription: Round silvery leaves — humidity-hungry but worth it.
calathea.description:
Orbifolia is the texture queen. Wide round leaves with silver stripes move at night.

Needs filtered water and steady 60%+ humidity. No drafts or direct sun.

For those ready to use a humidifier — stunning reward.

begonia-maculata.name: Polka dot begonia
begonia-maculata.shortDescription: Spotted leaves and red undersides — an Instagram star.
begonia-maculata.description:
Begonia maculata has angel-wing leaves with white dots on green. Red leaf undersides are signature.

Loves bright indirect light and even watering without standing water. Sensitive to dry winter air.

Place on an east window for a year-round show.

watering-guide.title: How to water houseplants in winter
watering-guide.excerpt: Five simple rules so roots do not die from cold and overwatering.
body: Winter watering is the top killer of plants in Kyiv and Lviv apartments. Shorter days slow photosynthesis while soil dries slower.
Check soil 2–3 cm deep with your finger. Dry — water with settled room-temperature water. Moist — wait 3–4 more days.
Do not water by calendar alone — water by plant condition. Snake plants and succulents may need water once a month in winter.
Empty the saucer after 20 minutes. Standing water at the roots leads to rot.

low-light-plants.title: 7 plants for rooms without sun
low-light-plants.excerpt: A north window is not a sentence. Picks for studios and hallways.
body: Low light does not mean no plants. Pothos, snake plant, peace lily, and ZZ are basics for dark corners.
Use labels: low — up to 2 h indirect sun, medium — bright indirect day, bright — east or west window.
Avoid total darkness without a lamp. Even 8 h of 4000K LED daily can save a fiddle leaf or monstera.

repotting-spring.title: Spring repotting: step-by-step
repotting-spring.excerpt: When, which pot, and which mix to choose for tropics.
body: Best repotting time is March–May when the plant wakes up. Avoid repotting a blooming begonia at peak flower.
New pot — 2–3 cm wider than the old one. Too much soil holds water and causes rot.
For monstera and philodendron — peat, perlite, bark 2:1:1. Succulents need a sandy mix.
No fertilizer for 4 weeks after repotting — let roots settle.

humidity-tips.title: Humidity without an expensive humidifier
humidity-tips.excerpt: Pebble trays, plant grouping, and misting — what works.
body: Radiators can dry air to 25% in winter. Calatheas and ficuses get crispy leaf edges.
Group plants — microclimate stays moister. A wet pebble tray under the pot is classic.
Mist in the morning, not evening. Water on leaves at night risks fungus.

pet-safe-plants.title: Pet-safe plants for cat owners
pet-safe-plants.excerpt: What will not harm your pet if they chew leaves.
body: Monstera and ficus are toxic to cats. Better — spider plant, peace lily (check ASPCA for your pet).
Keep pots on shelves or hanging planters. Mustard on the rim is a safe paw deterrent.
At Root & Leaf we tag “pet safe” on cards where it applies.

first-plant-kit.title: Starter kit: 3 plants for beginners
first-plant-kit.excerpt: Pothos, snake plant, and aloe — minimum stress, maximum green.
body: Do not buy 15 pots at once. Start with three types: trailing, upright, succulent.
Pothos teaches “water when it wilts”. Snake plant teaches patience. Aloe teaches sunny windowsills.
After 3 months add a monstera or peace lily when you feel the rhythm.
Clients in Odesa often pick this set for housewarming — 10% off the bundle in catalog promos.

reviews.text: Monstera arrived perfect with a Ukrainian care guide. Third month — a new leaf with splits!
Ordered snake plant for the office — water every three weeks, looks magazine-ready. Next-day delivery.
Pothos in a hanging planter — the only survivor in my dark bedroom. Support replied in 10 minutes.
I overwatered calathea at first, but support suggested a humidifier — it bounced back. Thanks for patience!
Large fiddle leaf, packed safely. Standing in the living room corner — guests ask where I bought it.
Spider plant for the kids room — safe and easy. My daughter waters it weekly herself.
ZZ in a windowless office — alive a year. Fair prices, no fake “premium” markup.
Read the winter watering journal — saved my whole balcony. Site is pleasant, not cluttered.
